corrections.caveats: SNIPPET ONLY: arxiv.org, ar5iv, proceedings.mlr.press, icml.cc (including the ICML 2022 slides PDF), hgpu.org, liner.com and ai.meta.com were EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the paper PDF was never opened; the table and setup (Flashlight 0.3.1, PyTorch 1.8, TensorFlow 2.4, Intel E5-2698 CPUs, V100-32GB GPUs in a DGX-1) come from WebSearch result excerpts of arXiv 2201.12465, and three separately worded searches (two by the search agent, one by the verifier) returned identical numbers for the rows they showed. The 512 GB RAM and NVLink details were not seen in the verifier's snippets. Peer-reviewed at ICML 2022 (a tier B candidate once the PDF can be read), but written by the Flashlight authors, so first-party. The repo's own benchmark tool (flashlight/app/benchmark: ModelBenchmarker.cpp, Run.cpp, models/AsrTransformer and LmTransformer) reports Flashlight-only V100 training throughput (ViT-Base, ResNet-34/50, DETR, LM and ASR transformers, FP32 and AMP, 1 to 32 GPUs) with no PyTorch or TensorFlow baseline; no AlexNet/VGG16 model and no PyTorch/TensorFlow comparison scripts were found in the repo, so the paper's comparison is not reproducible from public code. Compiler, flags, build options and framework configuration were not seen. The gains are under 10 percent on most rows (VGG16, ResNet-50 1 GPU, BERT-like, ASR, ViT), TensorFlow wins VGG16 on 1 GPU, and the large ratios come from AlexNet, a small, overhead-bound model. Framework versions date from 2021 (PyTorch 1.8, TensorFlow 2.4) and are far behind current releases. Times include data loading, so they are not pure kernel speed. Recent commits are mostly Meta fbcode sync and build fixes (CUDA 13 nvToolsExt fix 2026-09-14), not feature work. The awesome-cpp lead lists the license as BSD; GitHub shows MIT.

notes: Confirm at C: numbers match WebSearch snippets of the paper's Table 3 (AlexNet, VGG16, ResNet-50 rows checked; BERT-like, ASR and ViT rows not seen by the verifier), but the PDF was unreachable and the comparison scripts are not in the repo. Shortcomings: first-party paper read via snippets only; gains under 10 percent on most models and TensorFlow faster on VGG16 1 GPU; big ratios only on overhead-bound AlexNet; 2021 framework versions; timings include data loading; no public baseline scripts or flags.
